recognize_zh: 視野中絕大多數紅血球呈兩端鈍圓、邊緣平行的橢圓形或雪茄形（elliptocytes），比例明顯超過 30%，而中央淡染區仍保留、無明顯碎片或球形紅血球，符合遺傳性橢圓形紅血球症。
features: Majority of RBCs (well over 30%) are elliptocytes/ovalocytes with rounded ends and parallel sides, some elongated cigar or rod forms
RBCs are roughly normocytic with central pallor retained in many cells
No significant schistocytes, microspherocytes, or teardrop cells in this field
Scattered platelets of normal size and granularity
Single mature segmented neutrophil with normal granulation
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a striking population of elliptocytes and ovalocytes comprising well over 30% of red cells, including elongated rod- and cigar-shaped forms with smooth, rounded ends. Red cells otherwise appear approximately normocytic with preserved central pallor; fragments, microspherocytes and poikilocytes suggestive of pyropoikilocytosis are not prominent in this field. Platelets appear adequate in number and morphology, and the single neutrophil is unremarkable. In the setting of normal hemoglobin and iron studies, findings are consistent with hereditary elliptocytosis (common, likely mild/carrier phenotype).

ddx.vs: Iron deficiency shows hypochromic microcytic cells with thin elongated pencil cells in a minority of RBCs, whereas here the elliptocytes are normochromic and dominate the field with normal iron studies.
Teardrop cells taper to a single pointed tail and are accompanied by leukoerythroblastosis, unlike the symmetric rounded-end elliptocytes seen here.
HPP shows marked microcytosis with fragments, microspherocytes and bizarre budding poikilocytes and severe hemolysis, which are absent in this field.
SAO shows stomatocytic ovalocytes with one or two transverse slits or bars, whereas these elliptocytes lack slit-like central pallor.
